$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.17,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.17/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 25e559f64897c51faec74c7366d98649d023f228c6d72fcf06b3c0823dd5d983 and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.17/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
25e559f64897c51faec74c7366d98649d023f228c6d72fcf06b3c0823dd5d983 is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
